replies.author: @NovaTerrain-4K
replies.text: The segment on Caernarfon Castle [05:45] was profound. King Edward I built this massive stone fortress to crush independence and enforce assimilation, yet the Welsh responded right at its gates with the Mari Lwyd winter tradition—using a horse skull and satirical poetry to challenge authority. Did this ultimate contrast between colonial stone power and stubborn folk wisdom make you admire the resilient spirit of the Welsh?
